name: Typefully
tagline: Writing, scheduling, and analytics for X/LinkedIn threads and posts

pricing.notes: Official pricing URL checked; public 2026 references list Creator around $12.50/month annual-effective, with monthly pricing varying by plan.

verdictSummary: For personal thread drafting and scheduling, the core loop is vibecodable; the caveat is social API access, analytics, and platform-policy upkeep.
coreLoopDIY: Create a text editor for threads, preview character counts, store drafts, schedule via API, and track simple analytics.
whatYouLose: posting without paying X for API access
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the editor reduces friction and posting works without API babysitting.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source social scheduling prior art; can be adapted for thread workflows.

notes: The composer and queue are easy. The catch is X's API pricing — the write tier costs more than Typefully does. That's the moat: not code, a paywall.
prompt:
Build me a tweet composer and scheduler like Typefully. Requirements:

- A local web app: compose posts and threads with live character count per
  post, split threads with "---", drag to reorder, image attachments, and a
  clean distraction-free writing view with drafts autosaved to SQLite.
- A queue: pick a time or "next free slot" (slots defined in a config file,
  e.g. weekdays 9:00 and 16:00). Calendar-style queue view grouped by day.
- Publishing via the X API v2 (keys in .env) · with an honest README section:
  the free API tier is read-only; posting needs the paid tier, which costs
  more than Typefully. Include a fallback "copy thread to clipboard" button
  and a browser-notification reminder at slot time so the tool stays useful
  without paying X anything.
- A cron-style loop in the same process publishes due queue items and marks
  results (posted / failed with error).
- Single Node process, no accounts, runs on localhost or a VPS.
